pages.title: Syllabus Creation
pages.summary: Current YCCC syllabus template and a learning-centered syllabus checklist.

blocks.html:
Center for Teaching Excellence›Syllabus Creation

CTE Module

Syllabus Creation

Open the template ↗

Use the current YCCC template so students get the right college policies, contacts, and course information. A learning-centered syllabus is also a roadmap: it explains what students will learn, how they will be assessed, and how to succeed.

Current syllabus template

YCCC Syllabus Template V6 is ADA-compliant and includes the required college policy language.

Open template ↗

Submit a completed copy

Send the completed syllabus to YCCCsyllabi@mainecc.edu by the first day of the term.

Build a learning-centered syllabus

Use these questions as a final check before you share the syllabus with students:

  • Does the syllabus provide the information students need to succeed in the course?
  • Does it use the current YCCC template and current policy and contact information?
  • Does it encourage students to take personal responsibility for their learning?
  • Does it communicate key assignments and due dates so students can plan?
  • Does it state clear learning outcomes and high expectations for learning?
  • Are there sections from the sample syllabi that would work well in this course?
Need a syllabus review? CTE can review outcomes, assessment alignment, accessibility, and the student-facing language. Email ycccCTEsupport@mainecc.edu.

blocks.html:
Faculty Resources›Online Teaching

Faculty Resources

Online Teaching

Brightspace Support

Online and hybrid teaching work best when the course structure, communication, and support are intentional. Use these starting points before the term, during the term, and when you need help.

Before the term

Post the syllabus, organize modules in a predictable order, set up the gradebook, and check that every required tool opens correctly.

Open QuickStart videos

During the term

Use announcements and assignment feedback to keep students oriented. Check the gradebook regularly and follow through on Early Alert concerns.

Open Early Alert

When something breaks

For Brightspace errors, use the Brightspace Community or contact CTE Support. For student barriers outside class, use the Care Team.

Open Care Team

Teaching tools

  • Brightspace SupportCourse setup, grades, assignments, quizzes, rubrics, and advanced tools.
  • Brightspace QuickStartShort task-focused videos and training.
  • Faculty ToolboxMedia, accessibility, assessment, and virtual-classroom tools.
  • Instructional StrategiesUDL, backward design, and practical teaching resources.

Student support

  • Student Success CommonsTutoring, coaching, library, accessibility, and help.
  • Early AlertAcademic concerns: attendance, missing work, or grades.
  • Care TeamMental health, food insecurity, transportation, and other barriers.
  • Email CTE SupportCourse design, Brightspace, and teaching consultation.
Design for the students who are not in the room: Make directions explicit, keep the weekly rhythm predictable, and give students more than one way to ask for help.

pages.title: Academic Internships
pages.summary: Faculty-facing internship requirements, student eligibility, and program areas.

blocks.html:
Faculty Resources›Academic Internships

Faculty Resources

Academic Internships

Contact the Academic Dean

An academic internship is a curriculum-based, supervised work experience that enhances student learning. Students earn college credit through a faculty-sponsored experience guided by learning objectives, a YCCC faculty sponsor, and a qualified site supervisor at an approved work site.

What qualifies

Internships are semester experiences requiring at least 135 work-site hours for a 3-credit internship. Credit comes from the work-site experience plus academic work assigned by the faculty sponsor.

Student eligibility

Students must be matriculated in a degree program and meet the program's prerequisites. At minimum, YCCC requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA, 30 earned credits in the program, and permission of the Academic Dean.

Program areas

Academic internships are available across the college, including:

  • Accounting
  • Architecture & Engineering Design
  • Business Administration
  • Computer Aided Design
  • Computer Technology
  • Criminal Justice
  • Culinary Arts
  • Digital Media
  • Hospitality & Tourism
  • Museum Internship
  • Political Science
  • Precision Machining Technology
  • Psychology & Advanced Psychology
  • Writing/Communications

Key requirements

  • The internship must be a substantially different experience from any existing job duties with the same organization.
  • Students may be paid if the work site provides that benefit.
  • A family member cannot serve as the site supervisor, and the faculty sponsor and site supervisor must be different people.
  • Students pay tuition for registered credits; no course fees are assessed.
  • Credit is not awarded retroactively, and internships must begin and end within the standard academic calendar.
  • YCCC does not offer international internships.
Forms and full details: The legacy internship guide maintains the Academic Internship Contract, academic assignments, site handbook, and course outlines. Open the full internship guide ↗

Gender Equity

YCCC's Gender Equity program supports students enrolled in fields that are nontraditional for their gender—occupations in which less than 25% of one gender is enrolled or employed. The goal is the same educational and professional opportunity in every field.

  • Culinary Arts and Baking & Pastry
  • Architectural & Engineering Design
  • Computer Science and Information Technology
  • Trade and Technical Occupations

Nontraditional fields for men

  • Education
  • Health Studies
  • Veterinary Technology
  • Medical Assisting
  • Nursing

What the program offers

  • A supportive environment for students in nontraditional programs
  • Educational programs that empower men and women

pages.title: Prior Learning Assessment
pages.summary: Pathways for earning credit for college-level learning outside the traditional classroom.

blocks.html:
Faculty Resources›Prior Learning Assessment

Faculty Resources

Prior Learning Assessment

Legacy resource page ↗

YCCC recognizes learning that happens outside the traditional classroom—through work and volunteer experience, military training, workshops, professional certifications, and other approved pathways. Students must be formally admitted to a degree program and meet the program residency requirement.

Credit limits: Students may earn up to 75% of the credits required for graduation through all forms of prior learning combined. At least 25% of program credit hours must be completed directly through YCCC. Prior-learning credits count toward requirements but are not included in the GPA.

Prior learning options

  • Articulation agreements
  • Dual or concurrent enrollment
  • Military experience and training (ACE-evaluated)
  • Portfolio development
  • Professional certifications
  • Registered apprenticeship programs
  • Standardized exams (AP, CLEP, DANTES, IB, FLATS)
  • Transfer credit for previous courses
  • Workplace training (ACE-evaluated)

Examples of recognized credentials

YCCC's prior-learning review has recognized credentials and training including Adobe certified user credentials, Autodesk AutoCAD, Child Development Associate (CDA), Certified SolidWorks Associate, Cisco and CompTIA certifications, EMT Basic, Firefighter I and II, ISO 9001 Lead Auditor, Maine Criminal Justice Academy programs, Maine Roads to Quality credentials, MHRT-I, and ServSafe.

Start early: Requests for prior-learning credit should be made during the admissions process or shortly afterward so they can be considered in degree planning. See the full pathways and articulation list ↗
